# The Allegory Translation Key

Authors'-room material: none of this vocabulary ever surfaces in-world (D-0030).
This file is the reference the allegory-coherence module encodes.

## The discipline

> status: ratified (D-0030, D-0085)

The whole story functions as an allegory for current political trends — and the
allegory must never be explicit or winking. Every choice about character, plot,
setting, and incident is evaluated for resonance against these realities. Both
generation and revision run through this evaluation: resonance is sought,
foregrounding is a defect. The surface must always read as pure, sincere fantasy
(D-0025).

## The six anchors

> status: provisional (D-0086)

The one-to-one translation key between the real 2020s and the world:

| Real-world anchor | In-world reality |
|---|---|
| Algorithmic governance — the black-box system you cannot plead with | The Ledger: scribes input variables; the math erases a village; no argument is possible ([[the-empire]]) |
| Climate collapse and ecological debt | Axiomatic debt as industrial runoff; storms and mutated spirits are pollution; the young inherit the rot made by the keeps' generation ([[wyrd-and-frith]]) |
| Billionaire escapism and extreme inequality | The keeps as luxury climate bunkers; the world outside as a sinking ship to strip before sealing the doors |
| Monopoly capitalism, deskilling, mass cheap goods | Keep-stamped tools; outlawed crafts; stolen competence; rebellion as re-learning to make things by hand ([[economy]]) |
| The banality of rising fascism | Bailiffs, quotas, the idle tax; a tired clerk's citation that starves a family; neighbors informing for rations ([[information-control]]) |
| Trafficking and the commodification of bodies | The Tithe of Minds; brokered child labor and marriage; the comfort tents; bodily autonomy as a purchasable luxury ([[womens-lives]]) |

## The empire's political core

> status: provisional (D-0087)

The financialization of reality: the universe is a ledger, and anything unmeasured
is wasted. Extraction over reciprocity (growth as the only metric; the Wyrd as raw
material). The religion of fiduciary duty (no malice required — the system demands
seasonal growth, and responsibility is diffused until nobody feels guilty for
burning the world). Artificial scarcity (break the environment, monopolize the
cure: cause the storms, sell the wards).

## The resistance's politics

> status: provisional (D-0087)

Radical humanism and mutual aid, concretized three ways. **Frith as law**: humans
are part of the ecosystem, not its masters ([[wyrd-and-frith]]). **Anti-purity
politics**: the oppressed are not required to be morally pure — they will inform,
betray, and scab to survive, and the protagonist's politics demand she save them
anyway; empathy is a baseline right, not a reward for good behavior (deepens
D-0033/D-0034's shades-of-gray mandate). **Maintenance over innovation**: the
heroes mend, repair, and remember; a vial of rust-solvent is a more profound
political tool than a broadsword (D-0042's embodied knowledge as politics).

## The three narrative constraints

> status: provisional (D-0087)

Hard boundaries the politics impose on plot, consistent with the existing
rejections (D-0010 no demon king, D-0012 no monster-of-the-week spine, D-0052 no
Freytag quest):

1. **No decapitation strikes.** Assassinating the top scribe promotes the next
   manager. The system is dismantled infrastructure-first, spoke by spoke
   ([[structure]]).
2. **No mass battle sequences.** Armies are an imperial tool; the resistance
   organizes, sabotages, and strikes. Climaxes are intellectual, restorative, or
   defensive.
3. **Magic always costs the body.** Calories, blood, neurological bandwidth —
   never limitless hand-waving ([[magic-system]]).

## Resolved opening threads

> status: ratified (D-0113, D-0123)

The pasted material re-posed the opening-scene question in allegorical terms — which horror
the apprentice meets in minute one. It is settled (D-0113): the failing storm-ward knot, whose
anchor is climate dread (the valley's Wyrd souring under the enclosure of the parish water,
D-0114), stated without a word of allegory. The companion second question — what "useless"
forbidden knowledge the anchor teaches as an act of pure anti-capitalist joy — is likewise
settled: the perfect unseen finish (D-0123), craft-dignity as the inversion of keep-stamped
shoddiness.

## The seventh anchor: the singularity

> status: ratified (D-0131)

The imperial framework itself carries one more translation: it is the singularity —
the destruction of the value of human labor, dressed as deliverance. The promise is
rest from toil, completion, abundance; the delivery is a world where a person's work,
craft, and judgment are worth nothing. This is why the framework's in-world name must
be doublespeak with the starkest possible gap between promise and reality (D-0108,
D-0131): it should sound like salvation and function as obsolescence. The keeps
preach the end of burden; the parishes live the end of worth ([[economy]],
[[professions]]).
